runs.text: The business profile is adequate: diversified by technology but dependent on Alberta. The fleet spans hydro, wind, solar and gas in three countries and 53% of capacity is contracted for a weighted average of 9 years, yet Alberta produced 51.6% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA and 77% of Alberta capacity is exposed to the merchant market, so Alberta prices set the earnings that service debt. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 25

The financial profile is weakening on leverage but stable on liquidity. Last-twelve-months issuer-adjusted EBITDA fell 8.9% to CAD 1,006 million while debt at carrying value fell only 2.8%, so gross leverage rose from 3.93x to 4.19x and net leverage from 3.75x to 3.85x; these figures exclude the October 22, 2026 Colorado acquisition and Oklahoma wind sale, and pro forma net debt after them is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05

Interest cover is moderate rather than thin. Nine-month issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 3.80x cash interest paid, and free cash flow of CAD 338 million covered the CAD 100 million of common and preferred dividends paid 3.4 times, leaving CAD 238 million after dividends. A twelve-month cover is not available because full-year 2025 cash interest paid is not supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C08; calculation C09; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71

Liquidity and refinancing risk are low in the near term. Liquidity of CAD 1,867 million is more than four times the CAD 392 million of principal due by the end of 2027, no cash is drawn on committed facilities, and the syndicated and bilateral facilities were extended in July 2026. Instrument-level terms and covenant levels are not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40

Governance and sponsor risk is moderate. The cash price of the Colorado acquisition was paid with new equity, the dividend rose 8% and no extraction is documented, but five senior roles changed in 2026 and ownership percentages and debt documents are not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-06_q12026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-31_q22026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5

cells.text: One of Canada's largest publicly traded power generators with hydro, wind, solar, battery storage and gas, plus asset optimization and energy marketing.
Diversified technologies spread operating risk but earnings are driven by Alberta prices.
89 facilities with 8,623 MW of gross installed capacity: hydro 922 MW, wind and solar 2,587 MW, gas 5,114 MW.
Gas is 59% of capacity and 49% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA, so gas margins matter most.
Alberta 5,248 MW (61% of capacity); other regions 3,375 MW (United States 1,024 MW, Western Australia 498 MW, Canada outside Alberta 1,853 MW).
Alberta earned 392 of 759 million of nine-month adjusted EBITDA.
Contracted capacity 4,598 MW, 53% of total, weighted average contract life 9 years; Alberta contracted 23%, other regions 100%.
Contracts cover about half the fleet; Alberta is the merchant core.

77% of Alberta capacity is exposed to the merchant market; hedged production 2,061 GWh in Q4 2026 at $67 per MWh, 9,364 GWh in 2026 at $65 and 6,732 GWh in 2027 at $65; a $1 per MWh spot change moves 2026 Adjusted EBITDA by about $1 million.
Hedging and customer contracts dampen but do not remove Alberta price risk.
Five reportable segments from 2026: Hydro, Wind and Solar, Gas, Energy Marketing, Corporate; Energy Transition (Centralia) is no longer reportable.
Reporting change reflects the end of Centralia coal operations.
Nine months 2026 revenue of 1,588 million: contracts with customers 766, merchant sales 435, derivatives and trading 359, other 28.
About half of revenue is contract revenue; the rest depends on market prices and hedge results.

Centralia coal-to-gas conversion under a tolling agreement through 2044; Keephills data centre (Boreal Technology Hub) with initial PPA of about 230 MW and up to 1 GW of load evaluated; Colorado acquisition and Far North.
Projects lengthen contract life but need capital, approvals and counterparties.
Availability 92.6% in Q3 2026 against 92.7% a year earlier; production 5,260 GWh against 6,151 GWh with no Centralia production.
Fleet reliability is stable; volume fell with Centralia and Alberta dispatch optimisation.
Sheerness 1 mothballed April 1, 2026; Battle River 4 and 5 from March 1, 2027; Sundance 6 extended to April 1, 2029.
Avoids operating at low prices but leaves capacity waiting for contracts.

runs.text: Strength: liquidity and bank support. Cash of CAD 345 million and undrawn committed capacity of CAD 1,522 million give CAD 1,867 million of liquidity, no cash is drawn on committed facilities, and the July 2026 extensions to 2030 and 2028 remove near-term bank maturity risk, so a price shock would meet a large buffer. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40

Strength: a diversified, partly contracted fleet. Gas, wind and solar, hydro and marketing earn separately, 53% of capacity is contracted, and hedges are priced at $65 per MWh for 2027, which narrows the range of near-term cash flow. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 24

Strength: growth funded partly with equity. New equity paid the cash price of the Colorado acquisition and about 74% of principal falls due after 2030, although the Colorado project debt is not in that maturity ladder. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07

Weakness: leverage above the issuer's target and rising. The issuer measures 4.1x against a 3.0x to 4.0x target, and the 4.19x gross and 3.85x net ratios on issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose in 2026 because EBITDA fell faster than debt, which leaves little room for a further earnings fall before ratings pressure builds. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41

Weakness: merchant earnings and execution risk. Alberta provides 51.6% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA with 77% of its capacity merchant, Centralia has no generation under repeated federal orders, and four thermal units are mothballed or notified for mothballing while data-centre demand is unproven. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 12

Weakness: opaque debt terms. Covenant levels, instrument ranking, guarantors and the recourse of the US$750 million of Colorado project debt are not supplied, so creditor protection cannot be judged beyond the consolidated figures. Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

cells.text: TransAlta Corporation, incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act in March 1985, public since December 1992; head office Calgary, Alberta.
Common shares on the TSX (TA) and the NYSE (TAC); also NYSE-registered share purchase rights.
Primary Standard Industrial Classification code 4911; the run settings classify the sector as electric services.
Year ends Dec. 31; Ernst & Young LLP audits and attests to internal control.
316.3 million common shares at Nov. 2, 2026 against 296.7 million at the start of 2026; preferred shares series A, B, C, D, E and G.
Quarterly common dividend of $0.07 per share, $0.28 annualized, up from $0.26 annualized in 2025.
Joel Hunter, President and CEO from April 30, 2026; Mike Politeski, EVP Finance and CFO from May 1, 2026; Grant Arnold, EVP Growth and Chief Commercial Officer from May 6, 2026.
Nancy Brennan, Chief Legal, People and Corporate Affairs Officer, and Chris Fralick, EVP Generation and Chief Operating Officer, both from June 8, 2026.
Audit, Finance and Risk Committee of four independent directors, each an audit committee financial expert; Brookfield may nominate two directors.
S&P BB+ with negative outlook (July 24, 2026); Moody's Ba1 with stable outlook (June 18, 2026); Morningstar DBRS rating not stated.
Management concluded disclosure controls and internal control were effective at Sept. 30, 2026, excluding Far North; effective at Dec. 31, 2025.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Four transactions shaped 2026. Far North, four Ontario gas facilities of 310 MW, closed on Feb. 2, 2026 for CAD 95 million, or CAD 107 million with working capital adjustments, paid from cash and credit facility draws. The Colorado acquisition of two contracted gas peaking plants of 318 MW near Denver was agreed on June 3, 2026 and closed on Oct. 22, 2026 for US$1.0 billion, of which US$750 million is assumed project debt and US$250 million was funded by the June 2026 share offering of about CAD 350 million. A 49 per cent interest in the 500 MW Oklahoma wind portfolio was sold to Ares Infrastructure funds for US$305 million of cash on Oct. 22, 2026. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 77; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 98; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-07-31_q22026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5

No new senior notes or term debt were issued in the nine months to Sept. 30, 2026; the only debt-related action was the July 17, 2026 extension of the syndicated facility to 2030 and the bilateral facilities to 2028. The US$750 million of Colorado project debt is assumed rather than issued, and its lender, recourse and maturity are not established. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 40; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 70; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026newsreleasecombined.htm.jsonl, page 98

fields.value: Last-twelve-months issuer-adjusted EBITDA was CAD 1,006 million at Sept. 30, 2026 against CAD 1,104 million for FY2025, a fall of CAD 98 million, while gross debt at carrying value fell only CAD 123 million to CAD 4,220 million. The EBITDA fall is the same CAD 98 million nine-month decline: the Energy Transition segment, where Centralia stopped coal generation, lost CAD 90 million and Hydro lost CAD 48 million, partly offset by Gas, which gained CAD 32 million. Hydro and Gas revenues fell on lower Alberta spot and ancillary prices, net of favourable hedge pricing, while debt service is fixed, so leverage rises when merchant earnings soften.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and ownership risk looks moderate, but the business carries Alberta merchant-price exposure and execution risk on the Centralia conversion and data-centre plans, so creditors rely on contracted and hedged cash flow and on growth that is only partly equity-funded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alberta supplies 51.6% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA and 77% of Alberta capacity is exposed to the merchant market, while 53% of total capacity is contracted with a weighted average life of 9 years. Five senior roles changed in 2026, the cash price of the Colorado acquisition was paid with new equity, and the dividend rose 8% with no documented debt-funded distribution.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The profit pool is diversified by technology but concentrated in Alberta and gas. Gas earned CAD 374 million of the CAD 759 million nine-month adjusted EBITDA and Alberta CAD 392 million, so Alberta spot and ancillary prices drive results even though the fleet spans hydro, wind, solar and gas across Canada, the United States and Western Australia. A hedge position priced at $67 per MWh covers part of fourth-quarter 2026 Alberta production, which dampens but does not remove the exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management continuity is orderly but thin on history. The chief executive retired on April 30, 2026 and was succeeded by the chief financial officer, a new chief financial officer and chief commercial officer followed within a week, and two further senior roles changed on June 8, 2026. Four independent directors, all audit committee financial experts, sit on the audit committee, and internal control was assessed as effective at Sept. 30, 2026 excluding the Far North acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation has been acquisitive and partly equity-funded, not extractive. The June 2026 offering of about CAD 350 million funded the cash price of the Colorado acquisition, the Far North purchase of CAD 107 million used cash and credit facilities, the 49 per cent Oklahoma wind sale for US$305 million brings in cash, and no shares were repurchased in 2026 against CAD 24 million in the first nine months of 2025. The trade-off is project debt of US$750 million assumed with Colorado and an 8% higher dividend.

fields.value: No sponsor controls the company on the evidence supplied, but holder percentages are not established. Brookfield holds CAD 750 million of exchangeable securities, made up of CAD 350 million of 7% debentures due 2039 and CAD 400 million of preferred shares; they are exchangeable into the Alberta Hydro Assets at its option, it cannot call for repayment, and it may nominate two directors. A related-party power sale to Brookfield was small and fell in the first quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Execution and regulatory risk sit in three projects. The Centralia unit has had no generation in 2026 and runs under repeated 90-day federal orders whose costs are excluded from adjusted EBITDA and not yet recovered, the conversion needs about US$600 million of capital with a decision expected in early 2027, and the Alberta data-centre plans depend on approvals and definitive agreements while four thermal units are mothballed or notified for mothballing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a lower-risk reading is financial discipline: the cash price of the main acquisition was equity-funded, no extraction is documented, Brookfield's capital cannot be called, and the committed credit lines were extended in July 2026. The moderate rating would move higher if the Colorado project debt proves non-recourse and the data-centre agreement becomes a binding long-term contract, and lower if a debt-funded distribution, a further large acquisition without equity, or a failed Centralia approval appeared. Ownership percentages and creditor documents would also change it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four transactions shaped 2026. Far North, four Ontario gas facilities of 310 MW, closed on Feb. 2, 2026 for CAD 95 million, or CAD 107 million with working capital adjustments, paid from cash and credit facility draws. The Colorado acquisition of two contracted gas peaking plants of 318 MW near Denver was agreed on June 3, 2026 and closed on Oct. 22, 2026 for US$1.0 billion, of which US$750 million is assumed project debt and US$250 million was funded by the June 2026 share offering of about CAD 350 million. A 49 per cent interest in the 500 MW Oklahoma wind portfolio was sold to Ares Infrastructure funds for US$305 million of cash on Oct. 22, 2026.

fields.value: Governance and sponsor risk is moderate. The cash price of the Colorado acquisition was paid with new equity, the dividend rose 8% and no extraction is documented, but five senior roles changed in 2026 and ownership percentages and debt documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence that the profile is better than adequate is cash generation and guidance: the company reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA of CAD 950 million to CAD 1,050 million, needs only CAD 191 million in the fourth quarter to reach the low end, and paid its dividends from free cash flow with room to spare. If fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA exceeds the CAD 247 million of a year earlier, last-twelve-months EBITDA would rise above CAD 1,006 million, which would ease the 4.19x gross leverage if debt were unchanged. The view would weaken if Alberta prices fall further, if the Colorado project debt proves to be recourse, if the leverage ratio stays above the top of the issuer's target, or if S&P acts on its negative outlook.

fields.value: Overall, TransAlta presents an adequate business profile supported by diversified, partly contracted assets and strong liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by leverage above the issuer's target and Alberta merchant exposure. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covered dividends 3.4 times. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the extended bank facilities and the absence of large maturities before 2031. The primary downside path is a further fall in Alberta earnings combined with new acquisition debt. Further analysis would require covenant levels, instrument terms and the Colorado project debt terms.
